tasks.title: Make API and sync errors clear and actionable
tasks.desc: Review failures from TMDB requests and Neon synchronization; provide clear user feedback where the user can recover and useful diagnostics without exposing sensitive data. Add retry behavior only for transient, safe-to-repeat requests. Avoid a generic interceptor unless it fits the actual HTTP setup.

notes.text: Focused handling on observable API and synchronization failure modes.

Plan: trace where TMDB and Neon failures reach users, distinguish recoverable from background errors, then add clear actionable feedback and focused checks while preserving existing local data and retry safety.

TMDB and cloud-sync failures now show dismissible, accessible alerts with a safe recovery message; TMDB offers a page reload to repeat its read requests. Failure diagnostics now report operation and HTTP status without logging response bodies, URLs, or tokens. Local show data remains available after cloud failures. Verified 9 Jasmine tests and a production build; review that the notices are clear and that an explicit reload is acceptable for retrying catalog reads.

notes.text: Plan: capture a reproducible production build size report and browser performance measurements for the key routes; record environment, commands, limitations, and results so optimization tasks have a defensible baseline.

Baseline recorded for the production build. Reproduce with `pnpm exec ng build --configuration production --stats-json`; serve `dist/tv-time-calculator/browser` as static files (not `ng serve`), then record one local-browser navigation and the transfer sizes by resource type.
- Build: initial 519.10 kB raw / 128.78 kB estimated transfer, 19.10 kB above the 500 kB warning budget (below the 1 MB error budget). Auth component CSS is 6.05 kB, 2.05 kB above its 4 kB warning budget.
- Code splitting: route chunks are present (your-shows 68.51 kB; discover 35.01 kB; calendar 30.26 kB; top-series 29.43 kB; stats 26.87 kB; auth 22.60 kB). `withPreloading(PreloadAllModules)` in `src/main.ts` means they are fetched after startup; the local browser saw 13 JS files and one CSS file.
- One local static-build browser run on Windows: responseStart 25 ms, DOMContentLoaded 536 ms, load 1,440 ms; local assets transferred 737,664 bytes with compression disabled. Treat timings as a lab reference only, not production-user/Core Web Vitals data. The build output also contains `icon.avif` (1,330,006 bytes); this is emitted asset size, not evidence it was downloaded on the measured route.
- Checked Your Shows, Discover, Top 250, Calendar, and Stats screens. TMDB returned HTTP 401 in this local session, so catalog results and poster/image network usage were not representative. Repeat those measurements with working local TMDB credentials and a deployed/representative network before drawing conclusions.

tasks.title: Document codebase architecture and modules for AI context
tasks.desc:
Document the complete application architecture, module breakdown, and workflows so AI agents and new developers can quickly understand and navigate the codebase without ambiguity.

Scope includes:
1. High-level architecture and technology stack (Angular 19, standalone components, Tailwind, Netlify functions, Neon Postgres).
2. Directory structure and core modules (components, services, models, guards, utilities).
3. Data flow and state management (local storage vs. remote Neon Postgres sync, offline-first approach).
4. External APIs and integrations (TMDB/TVMaze endpoints, authentication, caching strategy).
5. Development, testing, and deployment workflows (environments, build, test commands).

Finished when structured documentation (e.g., in a `docs/` folder or root context guides) is established and ready for AI ingestion.

notes.text: Plan: 1. Survey the codebase architecture, models, services, components, Netlify functions, and sync logic. 2. Create structured, comprehensive documentation in docs/ and AI context files covering architecture, data flow, services, and developer workflows. 3. Verify documentation against the actual codebase.

Created comprehensive, structured documentation in `docs/` so any AI agent or human developer can immediately understand and navigate the codebase with complete clarity:

- `docs/AI_AGENT_GUIDE.md`: Dedicated guide for AI assistants containing the system mental model, 7 critical gotchas (e.g. SupabaseService naming, generated environment files, signals vs RxJS, instanceId format), and implementation playbooks.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: System design, tech stack (Angular 19, Tailwind CSS, Neon Postgres), layer architecture, and Mermaid system diagram.
- `docs/STATE_AND_SYNC.md`: Signal registry, two-tier storage (offline-first localStorage + Neon Postgres), conflict resolution, and TVMaze-to-TMDB legacy migration.
- `docs/API_AND_INTEGRATIONS.md`: TMDB v3 API contracts, in-memory caching, Netlify Functions (`/api/shows`), and local API server emulation.
- `docs/COMPONENTS_AND_ROUTING.md`: Complete component catalog, route table, guards, and modal interaction flows.
- `docs/DEVELOPMENT_AND_TESTING.md`: Environment setup, `set-env.js` automation, PWA service worker, and testing guidelines.
- `docs/README.md`: Central documentation index.
- Updated `AGENTS.md` and `README.md` with links and updated TMDB API references.

Verification:
- Executed `pnpm test` (all 11 unit tests passed).
- Executed `pnpm run build` (production build compiled successfully).

Check:

tasks.title: Validate input schemas and enforce payload size limits in shows function
tasks.desc: Add strict input validation to netlify/functions/shows.js. Enforce reasonable payload size limits, validate that item.show has a valid numeric ID, clamp user ratings between 0 and 10, ensure positive integers for seasons and episodes, and sanitize show_data JSON to store only necessary show metadata rather than arbitrary nested blobs. notes.text: Plan: inspect the shows endpoint, its existing tests and callers; implement bounded schema validation and sanitized metadata storage, then run focused checks.

Verified syntax plus an endpoint harness covering rejection-before-database, metadata stripping, nullable poster paths, and rating clamping.

notes.text: Plan: use an exact origin allowlist from Netlify URL, the production domain, and local dev origins; deny unapproved preflights and return generic client errors while retaining server logs.

Server failures now return only a generic 500 while detailed errors remain in server logs. CORS responses reflect only the configured Netlify URL, production domain, and local dev origins; disallowed/missing preflight origins receive 403 without an allow-origin header. Verified syntax, allowed and rejected preflights, allowed localhost, and hidden database details.

tasks.title: Implement rate limiting and request throttling for cloud sync endpoint
tasks.desc: Add protective rate limiting to prevent denial-of-service, quota exhaustion, and abusive write loops on /api/shows. Implement a sliding window or per-user request budget (returning HTTP 429 Too Many Requests when exceeded). Finished when rapid burst requests from a single user are safely throttled without impacting normal app usage.

notes.text: Plan: inspect normal sync burst behavior, apply a bounded per-user sliding-window limit to authenticated requests, expose Retry-After on 429, and add deterministic burst/reset tests.

Cloud sync now rejects oversized/malformed requests, stores whitelisted metadata, clamps ratings, sanitizes server errors, and restricts CORS. Authenticated requests are limited to 300 per user per rolling minute; excess requests receive 429 with Retry-After. Added pnpm test:api; all 7 tests and JavaScript syntax checks pass. Please review the validation and burst tests. Limiter state is per warm Netlify function instance, not shared across instances/cold starts; globally coordinated enforcement would need a shared store.
